title: First public playing at the Cotton Club with Jack Dupree
summary: With a mixed group at the Cotton Club he swapped piano and blues lessons with Dupree; he lists the Rampart Street clubs of the late 1930s.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: So what was the first time you tried to form a group? Was there a point where you tried to form a group? You know, first really get out and perform in front of people.

In front of people? Well, I got a chance to do that with, uh, well, we was working at the Cotton Club. We had a mixed group then. Let me see who was with us. We had Jack Dupreak with us then, because Jack Dupreak was singing in the community then. He wasn't playing music. I learned him a little bit about the piano and he learned me a little bit about the blues and singing lines. So we just transferred one thing to the other.
So you would teach each other.
You'd show him something, he'd show you something.

So the guy at the Cotton Club bought a piano. And, uh, I had been banging on the pianos and people at home and places and listening, like I see these clubs. So I figured I was good enough to take a chance in there because there wasn't nothing really happening no harm. Where was the Cotton Club? That was on Ramport between, uh, Caliope and Clio. Really? You had most of your big time clubs then. Around 37, 38, 39, most of your clubs was around in between Caliope and Clio on Ramport. You had the Cotton Club, you had the Dixie Bell, you had the Porter's Inn. You had a few little joints on the other side of the street. I can't remember the names right now.
